correctness.rationale: Use the 2026 Araya–Harada four [28,2,21]_4 projective-column seed vectors and Proposition 4.13 correspondence for [5s+3,2,4s+1]_4, s>=6. Adding a full PG(1,4) normalized projective line contributes J conjugate(J)^T=0 to the Hermitian Gram, so repeating the five-point block s-5 times preserves LCD. The four multiplicity lists have length 5s+3, minimum codeword weight 4s+1, no zero columns (dual distance>=2), and yield the four displayed weight enumerators by three scalar multiples per projective message direction. Monomial automorphisms are 3*prod_i(m_i!)*Stab_PGL(2,4)(m); PGL(2,4) acts as A5, and the multiplicity patterns have color-class partitions 2-1-2, 1-2-1-1, 3-1-1, 2-2-1 with even stabilizer orders 2,1,3,2 respectively. Thus factorial formulas A 6(s-1)!²(s+1)!(s+2)!², B 3(s-1)!s!(s+1)!²(s+2)!, C 9(s-2)!(s+1)!³(s+2)!, D 6(s-3)!(s+1)!²(s+2)!² follow. Independent GF4 implementation checked full GL(2,4) of order 180 and PGL of order 60, every color stabilizer and zero Hermitian Gram, while the inspected packaged certificate and verifier enumerate sample s=6,7,10. Exhaustiveness of the four code classes is explicitly imported from Araya–Harada, not independently proved by finite checks.
correctness.risk: The formula is for ordinary F4-linear monomial automorphisms, NOT semilinear equivalence; source classification supplies the exhaustive four-class statement.

value.rationale: Monomial automorphism-group orders are intrinsic coding invariants and appear explicitly in the mass formulas that substantiate the existing classification. The four full factorial forms for every s>=6 turn an automorphism calculation previously delegated to finite colored-graph computations into uniform, parameter-explicit symmetry data, distinguishing stable projective stabilizers 2/1/3/2. This is a natural complete four-class invariant even without a new code-construction theorem; not a free recomputation of a published numerical table.
